cards.explanation: The answer is False. The elders were summoned, but they didn't go up alone. Josiah, king of Judah, went up to the house of the LORD with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets too. The text says “…all the people small and great…” That's a whole crowd, friends, and not a committee.

The answer is read. In their hearing, Josiah read all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD. Not a summary and not the highlights. All the words, out loud, with everybody listening. Josiah doesn't skim the terms and conditions.

The answer is a covenant to follow the LORD. The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD “…to follow the LORD and to keep His commandments, decrees, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul…” Notice the words “…all his heart and all his soul…” That's a promise with nothing held back.

The answer is False. The king made the covenant by the pillar, and then the verse says, “And all the people entered into the covenant.” Josiah didn't keep it to himself or leave the crowd as spectators. They stepped into it with him, friends.

The answer is the articles made for Baal and Asherah. Josiah commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests second in rank and the doorkeepers to remove from the temple of the LORD “…all the articles made for Baal, Asherah, and all the host of heaven.” Baal and Asherah were false gods, and their things had no business in the LORD's house. I think that was a LOT of stuff to carry out.

The answer is burning incense to the sun and moon. These were idolatrous priests, ordained by the kings of Judah to burn incense on the high places. The text says they burned it “…to Baal, to the sun and moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.” Josiah did away with them.

The answer is that he burns it and grinds it to powder. The verse is plain about it. Josiah “…burned it, ground it to powder, and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.” He didn't stop at one step, friends. That's burning, grinding AND scattering, and I thought I was thorough when I sweep the counter twice.

The answer is desecrated. Josiah brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and desecrated the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where the priests had burned incense. That's a long stretch of ground, from one end to the other. Josiah's reach was wide.

The answer is True. The priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem. The text adds that they ate unleavened bread with their fellow priests. I'll let that sit there without adding anything of my own.

The answer is so no one could sacrifice a child to Molech. Josiah desecrated Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom “…so that no one could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the chapter. The text shows Josiah closing that place down.

The answer is False. Josiah removed the horses dedicated to the sun from the entrance to the house of the LORD. Then he burned up the chariots of the sun. No parade, no inheritance, and no extra ride for his army.

The answer is pulverizes. Josiah pulled down the altars on the roof near the upper chamber of Ahaz and the altars in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD. Then the verse says, “The king pulverized them there and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.” They went from altars to dust, friends.

The answer is King Solomon. It's right there in the text. Josiah desecrated the high places that “…King Solomon of Israel…” had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom. That's three gods of three different nations, the Sidonians, the Moabites and the Ammonites. Solomon, king of Israel, had built them.
The answer is True. Josiah smashed the sacred pillars to pieces and cut down the Asherah poles. Then he covered the sites with human bones. It's a heavy detail, and I'll leave it at that.
The answer is False. At Bethel, Josiah pulled down the altar, burned the high place and ground it to powder. Then verse 15 says he “…burned the Asherah pole.” The pole did not stay standing, friends.

The answer is that he burns them on the altar to defile it. Josiah saw the tombs on the hillside, sent someone to take the bones out, and burned them on the altar to defile it. The verse says this was “…according to the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these things.” It's a heavy scene, but the text ties it to that word.

The answer is the man of God who came from Judah. The men of the city told Josiah, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done to the altar of Bethel.” That's the man who had foretold all of this. Josiah looked at a tomb and heard that its owner had seen it coming.

The answer is False. Josiah said, “Let him rest…” and then, “Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” So they left his bones undisturbed, along with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria. That tomb was spared, friends.

The answer is that he removes them all just as at Bethel. The text says, “Just as Josiah had done at Bethel, so also in the cities of Samaria he removed all the shrines of the high places…” Those shrines had been set up by the kings of Israel who had provoked the LORD to anger. He took out all of them.
